Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark velvety fungal lesions on leaves and fruit, causing leaf distortion and premature drop.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply fungicides containing captan, mancozeb, or copper soaps at bud break. Remove and burn fallen leaves in autumn.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Prune tree canopies to maximize air circulation and sunlight penetration; plant scab-resistant cultivars.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Circular purple-bordered leaf spots ('frogeye'), cankers on limbs, and firm mummified rotting fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune infected cankers and dead branches 15 cm below infected tissue. Apply thiophanate-methyl or captan sprays.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Sanitize pruning tools between cuts. Clear mummified fruit hanging on twigs during dormancy.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surfaces; tube-like aecia structures forming on the underside.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Apply myclobutanil or sulfur sprays beginning at pink bud through petal fall.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Eradicate eastern red cedar galls within 1–2 miles of the orchard; select rust-resistant rootstocks.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No visible foliar lesions, spots, or chlorosis.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain balanced nitrogen/potassium fertilization, regular scouting, and dormant oil spray against overwintering scales.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green leaves with no necrotic margins or chlorotic mottling.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5–5.2) and mulch with pine needles or sawdust to retain moisture.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal mycelium covering young leaves, curling margins upwards, and stunting terminal shoots.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray horticultural oils, sulfur-based fungicides, or potassium bicarbonate at the first sign of mildew.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which produces susceptible tender tissue; prune inner shoots for airflow.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Clean, smooth foliage with uniform deep green color.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Ensure good soil drainage, avoid overhead irrigation, and prune regularly during dormancy.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Narrow rectangular tan lesions running parallel to leaf veins, eventually coalescing into blighted leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides (e.g., azoxystrobin + difenoconazole) at VT to R1 stage if threshold met.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops (soybean/alfalfa); till crop debris or use resistant corn hybrids.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Golden brown to cinnamon-brown pustules scattered across both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Fungicide application (pyraclostrobin or tebuconazole) when pustules appear before blister stage on susceptible lines.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrids; avoid late plantings that coincide with peak spore migration.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green lesions (2.5–15 cm long) with dark spore bands.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Apply systemic fungicides at the onset of lesions near tasseling.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Rotate crops for at least 1–2 years; deep-plow residue; plant hybrids carrying Ht resistance genes.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Uniform green canopy without fungal pustules or necrotic lesions.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Maintain optimal plant density and balanced soil fertility according to soil test recommendations.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots with dark margins and tiny black pycnidia; shriveled, hard black mummified berries.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Apply myclobutanil, azoxystrobin, or copper hydroxide from bud break through fruit set.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified clusters and infected canes during dormant pruning; manage trellis canopy for sunlight.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' chlorotic and necrotic patterns between leaf veins; dark speckled spots on berries.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: No cure once wood is infected; apply wound sealants or Trichoderma biocontrol to fresh pruning cuts.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Prune late in the dormant season to minimize wound exposure; destroy diseased grapevine trunks.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown patches on mature leaves leading to premature defoliation and weakened vines.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides or mancozeb during post-bloom periods.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Improve air drainage in the vineyard; avoid sprinkler wetting of leaf canopies.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Lush, well-developed green grape leaves with clean margins.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Regular canopy management, suckering, shoot positioning, and systematic pest scouting.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy yellow leaf mottling, yellow shoots, hard misshapen bitter fruit with aborted seeds.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: No cure exists; infected trees must be removed and destroyed to curb vector transmission.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Control the Asian citrus psyllid vector using targeted insecticides or parasitoid wasps; plant only certified disease-free nursery stock.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Water-soaked angular purple-brown spots on leaves, necrotic centers dropping out to create a 'shot-hole' appearance.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply protective copper sprays at bud swelling and oxytetracycline during the growing season.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation; avoid high-nitrogen fertilizers that produce vulnerable tender shoots; select resistant cultivars.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Intact lanceolate leaves without perforation or bacterial spotting.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Maintain balanced annual pruning and dormant fungicide sprays to prevent peach leaf curl.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked blister-like spots turning dark brown with yellow halos; severe leaf yellowing and dropping.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Spray fixed copper mixed with mancozeb, or use bacteriophage biocontrol solutions.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seed; hot-water seed treatment (50°C for 25 min); 2-year crop rotation away from Solanaceae.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Firm, deep-green foliage without lesions or curl.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Drip irrigation, reflective mulches to deter thrips and aphids, and proper calcium nutrition to avoid blossom end rot.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric rings ('target-board' pattern) on older leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin fungicides at regular intervals once symptoms appear.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Provide adequate nitrogen and potassium; practice 3-year crop rotation; avoid overhead irrigation.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions with pale-green borders; white fungal downy growth on the underside during humid conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Immediately apply systemic fungicides (e.g., metalaxyl, cymoxanil, mandipropamid). Destroy heavily infested vines before harvest.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers; monitor blight forecast tools; eliminate cull piles.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Robust, green compound leaves free of necrosis.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Hill up soil around stems properly to protect tubers; maintain balanced drip irrigation.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Normal serrated trifoliate leaves with vibrant coloration.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune out spent floricanes after harvest; ensure high trellis airflow.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Clean trifoliate leaves without mosaic, rust pustules, or frog-eye spots.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium; utilize minimum-tillage best practices; rotate with non-legume crops.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White talcum-like fungal powder covering leaf surfaces and stems, causing premature senescing.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray neem oil, potassium bicarbonate, sulfur, or triflumizole upon earliest symptom detection.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Space plants widely to facilitate air passage; select powdery-mildew resistant squash varieties.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small, irregular dark purple to reddish blotches that turn brown; entire leaf margins wither and appear scorched.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Apply captan, thiram, or dodine fungicides after planting and during post-harvest renovation.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Renovate beds by mowing old leaves after harvest; avoid excessive runner crowding and overhead watering.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous green trifoliate leaves with clean, crisp margins.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Mulch beds with clean straw to prevent splash dispersal; scout weekly for spider mites.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, greasy circular dark lesions with yellow halos; leaf yellowing and severe defoliation.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Spray copper fungicides combined with mancozeb; apply Actigard (acibenzolar-S-methyl) for plant defense induction.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds; sanitize stakes and cages; eliminate nightshade weeds around fields.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown to black lesions with characteristic concentric rings, usually beginning on the lowest leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, copper soap, or difenoconazole every 7–10 days upon detection.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Mulch heavily at base to prevent soil splashing; stake plants and prune lower sucker branches.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular oily olive-brown lesions; white fuzzy mold on leaf undersides in wet weather; rapid collapse.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Spray protective fungicides (chlorothalonil, mancozeb) proactively; use translaminar fungicides if disease arrives.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid planting tomatoes near potatoes; water early morning via drip irrigation; dispose of blighted vines in sealed bags.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow patches on leaf surfaces matching olive-green to brown velvety mold on the underside.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Apply copper sulfate or bio-fungicides (Bacillus subtilis); increase ventilation in greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Keep greenhouse relative humidity below 85%; space plants generously and prune bottom foliage.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (1.5–3 mm) with grayish-white centers and dark brown borders, dotted with black speck pycnidia.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Treat with chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper fungicides at the first sign on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Rotate away from solanaceous crops for 3 years; prune lowest 30 cm of foliage to keep leaves off the soil.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on leaf surfaces, delicate fine silk webbing between leaves, leading to bronze desiccated foliage.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, abamectin, or bifenazate miticides. Ensure thorough underside coverage.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis); avoid water stress; wash leaf undersides with strong water spray.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Pinpoint brown spots enlarging into target-like circular necrotic lesions with light brown centers.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Apply azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin, or fluopyram fungicides.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Eliminate weeds; provide wide row spacing; avoid prolonged leaf wetness through drip lines.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe upward leaf cupping, chlorotic leaf margins, severe plant stunting, and bushy upright growth with no fruit set.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: No cure; remove and destroy symptomatic plants immediately to prevent whitefly vector spread.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Manage sweetpotato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) with yellow sticky cards and systemic imidacloprid; plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic mottling, leaf distortion ('shoestringing'), and blistered leaf surfaces.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No chemical cure; remove infected plants immediately and disinfect all tools with 20% non-fat dry milk or trisodium phosphate.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Wash hands with soap before handling plants (especially smokers, as tobacco carries related tobamoviruses); use resistant seeds.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant, green compound leaves free of discoloration, curling, or lesions.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular watering to prevent blossom end rot; prune suckers for airflow and stake firmly.
